title: Resolving models for finite-reduction pullback and strict derived tower pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites put $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}S_{W,n}$, $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$, with specified projections $\pi_{W,n}$ and quotient transitions $q_{n+1,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. All finite levels are restricted along these projections. Write $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$ for the projection-induced ring map and $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}R_{T'}$ for ordinary module pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Use unbounded cochain complexes and their derived localizations $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A good complex means K-flat with flat terms [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. Set $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with transition $(t,1)$ and augmentation $\epsilon_{W,n}:Q_{W,n}\to S_{W,n}[0]$ equal to $\pi_{W,n}$ in degree zero and zero in degree minus one [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers].

Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the full homotopy subcategory of good $R_T$-complexes. On all complexes let $F(P)_n=P\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n}$ and $B_g^0(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*F(P)_n$, with the actual quotient transitions; finite module pullback $g_n^*$ is that of [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback], and $B_g^0$ is the strict construction of [def-a1-integral-finite-pullback-tower]. Write $\operatorname{Tow}_{R_W}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(R_W))$, $\mathcal R(K)=K_\bullet$ for strict derived reduction and $V_g=LG^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ for strict derived tower pullback [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

The construction $B_g^0$ respects chain homotopies, shifts and mapping-cone complexes and sends every quasi-isomorphism between good complexes to a levelwise quasi-isomorphism of strict towers. There exists an everywhere defined left derived pair $(B_g,\beta)$ with $B_g:D(R_T)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_{R_{T'}})$ and universal counit $\beta:B_gQ\to QB_g^0$, invertible on good complexes. For each good $P$, set $H(P)_n=P\otimes Q_{T,n}$ and $a_P=(1_P\otimes\epsilon_{T,n})_n:H(P)\to F(P)$. This is a strict quasi-isomorphism, natural in chain maps, with source levels good, source transitions $1_P\otimes(t,1)$ and target transitions the actual quotients. The reduction computation identifies $QF(P)=\mathcal R(QP)$, and the canonical tower-pullback computation is
$$\chi_P=\varepsilon^{V}_{H(P)}\circ V_g(Qa_P)^{-1}:V_g(\mathcal R(QP))\xrightarrow{\sim}QGH(P),$$
where $\varepsilon^{V}$ is the universal left-derived counit of $V_g$. Both $\chi_P$ and $\beta_P$ are natural for chain maps between good complexes. These are computations of entire strict towers indexed by the small category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$. No exactness of $G$ or invertibility of $c_g$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the normalized finite-reduction additive compatibility theorem for homotopies, shifts, cones, inclusion and connecting-map equations. This is exactly step 1 isolated from the resolving-class and Koszul arguments.

For a quasi-isomorphism of good complexes, use finiteReduction_quasiIso on each actual quotient. Apply the exact additive finite coefficient pullback and the exact scalar restriction. The evaluation criterion for quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of functors gives the whole-tower assertion.

Use the proved functorial_resolution with K-flat outputs and flat terms. Apply deriveFromFunctorialResolution to the localized strict finite-pullback functor and the good-complex object property. The previous inversion assertion supplies its hypothesis. Obtain the universal derived pair and computation on every good complex.

Apply principal_koszul_strict_replacement to each good P. Its augmentation is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism and every source level is good. The evaluation criterion makes the transposed augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. Its naturality is the existing strict comparison_naturality equation.

Use the canonical scalar-normalized strict quotient-tower isomorphism N. Map it by transposition and Q and compose with the inverse of the reductionPair counit on P. This gives reductionIso r with r.hom followed by the counit equal to Q(N.hom), hence fixes its normalization. Naturality follows from N and the counit, cancelling the invertible counit.

The towerPull_exists computation criterion applies to the K-flat source levels. Thus the actual derived tower-pullback counit on the Koszul tower is invertible. The localized augmentation is invertible as well. Define a as Q(augmentation) followed by r, and chi as derivedPull.mapIso(a.symm) followed by the actual derived counit. This yields the specified chi formula in the entire strict-tower derived category.

Combine strict augmentation naturality with reductionIso naturality to obtain naturality of a. Precompose the desired chi equation with derivedPull.map(a.hom), cancel the inverse isomorphisms, and apply derivedCounit.naturality. Beta naturality is the naturality field of the universal counit constructed above.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q140-7648e33ad (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 8 steps and every cited statement in full, plus Stacks 06XN (derived.tex lines 5092-5117, dual LF part). No new nodes and the statement is unchanged. Not superseded: the item is unsplit with no proof on both live and side-live, and it is not on the drop list. No cycle; no SGA.
Step 1: a termwise additive A_n preserves homotopies, shifts and cone matrices. Step 2: the change-of-rings K-flat lemma applies to π_n; finite-constant exactness covers any g; Res and levelwise cohomology finish it. Step 3: K-flat resolution plus the resolving-class theorem give (B_g, β), with β invertible on good complexes. Step 4: the sfb normalization lemma gives the ring isomorphism to the limit identifying the projections, K-flatness of [R→t^n R] and the exact-q augmentation quasi-isomorphism. Step 5: the total-tensor lemma makes H(P) good, and the fixed-good-factor lemma makes 1⊗ε_n a quasi-isomorphism. I re-checked that (t,1) is a chain map and that the augmentation square commutes. Step 6: the datum's K-flat computation applies, and (A,(t)) meets its hypotheses (Noetherian, finite perfect quotients, A/t finite hence torsion). Step 7: the diagram replacement lemma with J = N^op and c_g, plus the resolving-class theorem, gives ε^V invertible on objectwise-good towers, without exactness of G. Step 8: I re-derived the naturality algebra and it is correct.
Edge cases checked: P=0, P=R[0], n=1, g=id, unbounded P, non-flat c_g. Accepted the generic tool uses; the levelwise-abelian entry is unneeded because that node is a Mathlib leaf.
Maintainer notes: (1) the item applies the A_T-datum and V_g to R_W = lim of constant sheaves. This convention is inherited from the item's statement and its reviewed parent. The two presentations agree canonically, but stage 2 should use the def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport e/Φ transport if the Lean rings differ. (2) lem-sf-completed-coefficient-free-resolution would be a more direct cite for step 4. (3) lem-a1-principal-augmented-roos-descent overlaps steps 4-6 at the proof level only.
